sources.title: Poestenkill rejects sheriff's office proposal for license plate readers at Town Hall

Current store listings establish candidates, not historical proposal identity.

data.question: Which public Stewart’s property records can narrow the unresolved Hudson Police ALPR proposal without guessing the site?
data.method: Reused the existing Hudson-proposal target, checked the prior #1902 packet, reconciled local reporting, and enumerated Stewart’s current first-party Hudson directory.
data.framework: reported proposal -> candidate property universe -> first-party labels -> native proposal required for identity resolution
data.scope: Separate Hudson Police / Columbia County Stewart’s ALPR proposal only; no deployment inference.
findings: Stewart’s current first-party Hudson directory lists Claverack #493 at 811 NY-66, Greenport #239 at 5805 Route 9G, and Hudson Rt 9 & Fairview Ave #209 at 13 Fairview Avenue.
Shop #209 is the only one of those three whose first-party store label itself is Hudson Rt 9 & Fairview Ave; it is a records-search priority, not proof of proposal selection.
Times Union reporting establishes that Hudson Police made a similar Stewart’s request in Columbia County and that Stewart’s rejected it, but does not identify the property.
conclusions: The exact Hudson proposal site remains unresolved.
All three Hudson-addressed entries should be searched in native records, with #209 prioritized but not promoted.
The proposal remains a rejected proposal, not a deployment.
recommendations: Recover Hudson Police and Stewart’s correspondence, proposal/quote, site plan, or Flock location identifier.
Search records for 13 Fairview/shop 209, 5805 Route 9G/shop 239, and 811 NY-66/shop 493.
Record excluded candidates as counterevidence when native records identify the site.
counterarguments: The current directory is September 2026 evidence and cannot independently resolve an August-December 2025 proposal.
limitations: No native proposal or rejection correspondence naming the site was recovered.
unresolved: Which exact Stewart’s property did Hudson Police propose?
What equipment, ownership, maintenance, platform-access, and data-control terms accompanied the proposal?
What native record documents Stewart’s rejection of that specific site?
